objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic vulvar itching and discomfort.

fragments.text: The patient presents with a complaint of severe vulvar itching that has been gradually worsening over the course of the past year. She has attempted to use over-the-counter lubricants for relief with no substantial improvement. She reports severe pain during vaginal intercourse that has recently led to cessation of sexual activity.
Use of over-the-counter lubricants with no relief
Diet-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide, menopause occurred at 52 years of age.
Sexually active with her husband until recently due to discomfort.
Denies urinary symptoms, abnormal vaginal discharge, or rectal symptoms.

exam_leaves.text: Dry, thin, white plaque-like lesions in the vulvar area, with atrophy of the labia minora. The clitoris appears retracted. The perianal skin is pale and wrinkled.
The lesions are palpable and the vulvar area is tender to touch.

test_leaves.text: Hyperkeratosis with thinning of the epidermis and sclerosis of the dermis, confirming lichen sclerosus.
